content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published a second edition of its guidelines for the screening and treatment of cervical pre-cancer lesions to prevent cervical cancer. This document is available in both electronic and print formats, with respective ISBNs 978-92-4-003082-4 and 978-92-4-003083-1. The publication is copyrighted by WHO in 2021, and its content can be copied, redistributed, and adapted for non-commercial purposes, provided proper citation is given. WHO is not liable for any damages arising from the use of the material. The guidelines were developed with contributions from various groups, including the Guideline Development Group (GDG), the External Review Group (ERG), and other external contributors. The process was supported by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), which provided literature reviews, and by systematic review teams coordinated by Nancy Santesso from McMaster University. The GDG identified screening tests and clinical algorithms for evaluation, prioritizing seven algorithms for systematic review. Mathematical modeling was also employed to assess the impact and cost-effectiveness of different screening and treatment strategies. The updated guidelines aim to simplify algorithms and increase access to screening and treatment to meet the 2030 targets outlined in WHO's Global Strategy for the elimination of cervical cancer. These targets include achieving 90% HPV vaccination coverage among eligible girls, 70% screening coverage with a high-performance test, and 90% appropriate management of women with positive screening results or cervical lesions. The guidelines include 23 recommendations and 7 good practice statements. Among the recommendations, 6 are identical for both the general population of women and women living with HIV, while 12 are specific to each group. The recommendations are based on evidence synthesized through systematic reviews and the application of the GRADE methodology, which assesses the certainty of evidence and develops recommendations using evidence-to-decision (EtD) tables. The screening and treatment approaches outlined in the guidelines include two main strategies: the screen-and-treat approach, where treatment decisions are based solely on a positive primary screening test, and the screen, triage, and treat approach, where treatment decisions are based on a positive primary screening test followed by a positive secondary (triage) test, with or without histological confirmation. The guidelines were developed in accordance with the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (second edition, 2014) and involved extensive collaboration among experts, technical groups, and the WHO Secretariat. The process included the integration of systematic reviews prepared for IARC's Handbooks of Cancer Prevention, Volume 18 (2021), which focused on cervical cancer screening. Additionally, studies on the acceptability, feasibility, and cost of the proposed algorithms were reviewed, and surveys were conducted to gather insights on feasibility, values, and preferences from service users. The publication acknowledges the contributions of numerous individuals and organizations, including members of the GDG, ERG, systematic review teams, and modeling groups. Special thanks are extended to the WHO Guidelines Review Committee Secretariat and the WHO Steering Group for their support throughout the guideline development process. Funding for the preparation, development, and printing of the guidelines was provided by the UNDP-UNFPA-UNICEF-WHO-World Bank Special Programme of Research, Development, and Research Training in Human Reproduction (HRP), with additional support from the United States President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) through USAID and Unitaid.
